title: The widow's jar (1 Kings 17:8–16)
hookLine: a widow shares her last flour, and the jar never runs out

cards: At the gate of a town called Zarephath, a woman is gathering sticks. Not many. Just enough for one small fire.
A stranger, dusty from the road, calls out to her: bring me a little water in a vessel, so I can drink. She turns to get it. Then he calls after her: and bring me, please, a piece of bread.
She stops. Her answer is blunt, and it tells you everything about her kitchen.

teach.h: A WIDOW IN ZAREPHATH OF ZIDON.
teach.b: Zarephath belongs to Zidon, outside the land of Israel.

teach.h: A HANDFUL OF MEAL, A LITTLE OIL.
teach.b: She answers Elijah with an oath, as the LORD your God lives, and then the plain truth: nothing baked, only a handful of meal in a jar and a little oil in a cruse.
She's gathering sticks to make one last meal for herself and her son, so they can eat it and die. The Hebrew word for her jar is kad. Elijah says: don't be afraid.
Go and do as you said, but make me a little cake first, and after that make some for yourself and your son.

teach.h: ENOUGH, EACH DAY, UNTIL THE RAIN.
teach.b: For the LORD has said the jar of meal won't be used up and the cruse of oil won't fail until the day the LORD sends rain. Hear what he's asking. Her last flour.
To a stranger. Before her own child. And she does it.

teach.h: NEITHER DID THE CRUSE OF OIL FAIL.
teach.b: She, and he, and her house ate for many days, and in the 1917 Jewish translation: "The jar of meal was not spent, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD."
Each day she reaches into a jar that should be empty, and there's enough for that day. Not a mountain of flour. Enough.

Notice who this miracle runs through: not a king, not a priest, but a widow in a town of Zidon, at the end of her supplies, who shares first. Ravens fed Elijah; now a woman with nothing to spare feeds him.
Giving, in this story, doesn't start with plenty. It starts with a handful.

how: Jews read the story of the widow of Zarephath in the book of Kings, where it is followed in the same chapter by Elijah's prayer for her son.

games.q: you have one handful of flour left for you and your son. a stranger asks you to bake for him first. what do you do?

give him the flour and let him bake.
games.why: she went and did as Elijah said, and the jar of meal didn't run out and the cruse of oil didn't fail.

practice: Name what feels scarce for you right now, time, money, energy, patience, honestly, the way the widow did at the gate.
Then think of one small thing you could still share from it, not from the surplus but from the handful, and let that thought settle. If you pray, you can ask for some of her courage.

wordCard.voice: Kad. The Hebrew word for jar, the one with a widow's last flour that never ran dry. Today's word.
